'''''Quercus coccifera''''', commonly known as '''kermes oak''', '''holly oak''', or '''Palestine oak''',<ref name="IOS">{{cite web |title=Are Quercus calliprinos and Q. coccifera the Same or Distinct Species? |website=International Oak Society |date=4 December 2023 |url=https://www.internationaloaksociety.org/content/are-quercus-calliprinos-and-q-coccifera-same-or-distinct-species |access-date=11 November 2024 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Quercus coccifera subsp. calliprinos {{!}} Palestine oak /RHS |url=http://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/120662/quercus-coccifera-subsp-calliprinos/details |access-date=2026-02-04 |website=www.rhs.org.uk |language=en-gb}}</ref> is an evergreen [[oak]] shrub or tree in [[section (botany)|section]] ''[[List of Quercus species#Section Ilex|Ilex]]'' of the genus.<ref>{{Citation |last1=Denk |first1=Thomas |chapter=An Updated Infrageneric Classification of the Oaks: Review of Previous Taxonomic Schemes and Synthesis of Evolutionary Patterns |date=2017 |chapter-url=https://www.biorxiv.org/content/biorxiv/early/2017/07/31/168146.full.pdf |title=Oaks Physiological Ecology. Exploring the Functional Diversity of Genus Quercus L. |pages=13–38 |editor-last=Gil-Pelegrín |editor-first=Eustaquio |place=Cham |publisher=Springer International Publishing |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-319-69099-5_2 |isbn=978-3-319-69099-5 |access-date=16 November 2022 |last2=Grimm |first2=Guido W. |last3=Manos |first3=Paul S. |last4=Deng |first4=Min |last5=Hipp |first5=Andrew L. |editor2-last=Peguero-Pina |editor2-first=José Javier |editor3-last=Sancho-Knapik |editor3-first=Domingo }}</ref> It has many [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonyms]], including '''''Quercus calliprinos'''''.<ref name=POWO_295963-1/> It is native to the [[Mediterranean region]] and Northern African [[Maghreb]], south to north from Morocco to France and west to east from Portugal to Cyprus, [[Anatolia]], and the [[Levant]], crossing Spain, Italy, Libya, the [[Balkans]], and Greece, including [[Crete]]. The Kernes oak was historically important as the food plant of ''[[Kermes (insect)|Kermes]]'' scale insects, from which a red [[dye]] called crimson was obtained.<ref>{{cite book |last=Young |first=Frank N. Jr |title=A Survey of Entomology |year=2002 |publisher=Writers Club Press |location=San Jose |isbn=0-595-22143-2 |page=9 |author2=Kritsky, Gene }}</ref> The etymology of the specific name ''coccifera'' is related to the production of red cochineal (crimson) dye and derived from Latin [[wikt:coccum#Latin|coccum]] which was from Greek [[wikt:κόκκος|κόκκος]], the kermes insect. The Latin [[wikt:-fera#Latin|-fera]] means 'bearer'.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.thefreedictionary.com/cochineal |title=Cochineal }}</ref>

==Description==
''Quercus coccifera'' is usually a [[shrub]] less than {{convert|2|m|ft|abbr=off|frac=2}} high, rarely a small tree, reaching {{convert|1|-|6|m|frac=2|ft}} tall (with {{convert|10|m|ft|abbr=on|disp=or}} specimens recorded in [[Kouf]], Libya).<ref>{{cite web |title=Important bird areas fact sheet: Jabal al Akhdar |url=http://www.birdlife.org/datazone/sitefactsheet.php?id=6471 |publisher=BirdLife International |access-date=22 June 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222002630/http://www.birdlife.org/datazone/sitefactsheet.php?id=6471 |archive-date=22 February 2014 }}</ref><gallery>

File:Quercus coccifera severely stunted growth habit Mount Attavyros Rhodes.jpg|Severely stunted ''Q. coccifera'' due to intense wind and grazing pressure on [[Attavyros|Mount Attavyros]], Rhodes. ( It is the reddish tipped shrub)
</gallery>

== Taxonomy ==
===''Quercus coccifera''===
''Quercus coccifera'' was first described by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in 1753.<ref name=POWO_295963-1/> It is called "[[wikt:chêne des garrigues|chêne des garrigues]]" (garrigue oak) in French. The term "[[wikt:garrigue#French|garrigue]]" comes from Catalan or Occitan "[[wikt:garric|garric]]" (meaning "twisted") the name for ''Q. coccifera'' in those languages. A common Spanish name of ''Q. coccifera'' is ''[[wikt:chaparro#Spanish|chaparro]]'', which refers to its small size, a feature it shares with other oak species in similar habitats in other parts of the world, such as the [[chaparral]] communities from various parts of the Americas. The word ''chaparro'' comes from the [[Basque language|Basque]] ''[[wikt:txapar|txapar]]'' meaning "little thicket".<ref>{{cite web |title=chaparral |url=http://www.etymonline.com/index.php?allowed_in_frame=0&search=chaparral&searchmode=none |access-date=22 June 2013 |work=Online Etymology Dictionary |publisher=Douglas Harper }}</ref> ''Quercus coccifera'' is placed in [[Quercus sect. Ilex|section ''Ilex'']].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Denk |first1=Thomas |last2=Grimm |first2=Guido W. |last3=Manos |first3=Paul S. |last4=Deng |first4=Min |last5=Hipp |first5=Andrew L. |date=2017 |title=Appendix 2.1: An updated infrageneric classification of the oaks |website=figshare |doi=10.6084/m9.figshare.5547622.v1 |url=https://figshare.com/articles/dataset/Appendix_2_1_________An_updated_infrageneric_classification_of_the_oaks/5547622/1 |access-date=18 February 2023 |format=xls |name-list-style=amp }}</ref>

===''Quercus calliprinos''===
{{As of|2023|February}}, [[Plants of the World Online]] regards it as a [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]] of ''Quercus coccifera'',<ref name=POWO_295963-1/> but this is widely disputed, with many authors, particularly in the eastern Mediterranean, considering it distinct at least at [[subspecies]] rank, if not as a species.<ref name="IOS"/><gallery mode="nolines" widths="200" heights="200">
File:Quercus coccifera spp calliprinos UC Davis Arboretum.jpg|Quercus calliprinos subspecies has flatter leaves.
</gallery>

== Conservation==
It is included as an endangered species in the Red Book of Bulgaria.<ref>{{cite web |title=Quercus coccifera |url=http://e-ecodb.bas.bg/rdb/en/vol1/Quecocci.html |access-date=19 January 2017 |website=Red Book of Bulgaria, vol. 1 }}</ref>
